```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Load Libraries

library(CVXR)

```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
project_dir <- getwd()

knitr::opts_knit$set(
  root.dir = normalizePath(
    file.path(project_dir, "..", "..")
  )
)
```

For this model, we will use two basics training and testing datasets:

* `prediction_dataset.csv`: For prediction purposes

* `regression_dataset.csv`: For training and regression purposes

### Load dataset
```{r}
# Regression Dataset
regression_data <- read.csv("data/training_data/regression_dataset.csv")

regression_data$population <- regression_data$population * 1000

# Prediction Dataset
prediction_data <- read.csv("data/training_data/prediction_dataset.csv")

# National GDP totals used to constrain the regression fit
constrained_data <- read.csv("data/_vnm_indicators/vnm_level0_gdp.csv")

# Provincial GRDP per-capita targets used to calibrate 2025 level-2 predictions
provincial_grdp_data <- read.csv(
  "data/_vnm_indicators/vnm_GRDPpc.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Provincial population totals (thousands) used as the aggregation constraint
provincial_population_data <- read.csv(
  "data/_vnm_indicators/vnm_population.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
```


### Preliminaries
Supposed:

* \(y \in \mathbb{R}^n\): observed outcome vector. That is, `grdp_per_capita`.
* \(x_i \in \mathbb{R}^3\): standardized explanatory variables for observation \(i\): `mean_radiance`, `population`, and `pixel_count`.
* \(\alpha_t \in \mathbb{R}\): year-specific intercept for year \(t\).
* \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^3\): shared slopes for the explanatory variables.
* \(a_t \in \mathbb{R}\): specified national GDP total for year \(t\).

The model includes a separate intercept for each year and shared slopes for the
explanatory variables. The constraints ensure that population-weighted
predictions match the national GDP target for every year.

```{r}
# Definitions
y <- regression_data$grdp_per_capita
years <- sort(unique(regression_data$year))
regression_data$year_factor <- factor(regression_data$year, levels = years)

feature_columns <- c("mean_radiance", "population", "pixel_count")
feature_means <- vapply(regression_data[feature_columns], mean, numeric(1))
feature_sds <- vapply(regression_data[feature_columns], sd, numeric(1))
if (any(!is.finite(feature_sds)) || any(feature_sds == 0)) {
  stop("Training predictors must have finite, non-zero standard deviations.")
}

scaled_feature_columns <- paste0(feature_columns, "_scaled")
for (feature in feature_columns) {
  scaled_feature <- paste0(feature, "_scaled")
  regression_data[[scaled_feature]] <-
    (regression_data[[feature]] - feature_means[[feature]]) /
    feature_sds[[feature]]
}

X <- model.matrix(
  ~ 0 + year_factor + mean_radiance_scaled + population_scaled +
    pixel_count_scaled,
  data = regression_data
)

p <- ncol(X)
year <- regression_data$year
population <- regression_data$population

target_gdp <- constrained_data$gdp[match(years, constrained_data$year)]
if (anyNA(target_gdp) || any(!is.finite(target_gdp))) {
  stop("Missing or non-finite national GDP target for one or more model years.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(constrained_data$year[constrained_data$year %in% years])) {
  stop("National GDP data contains duplicate targets for a model year.")
}
```

### Optimization problem

The optimization problem is
\[
\boxed{ 
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\alpha,\beta}\quad & \|y-\hat y\|_2^2\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
&\sum_{i:\,\mathrm{year}_i=t} P_i\hat y_i=a_t,
\quad t\in\{2020,\ldots,2025\},\\
&\hat y_i=\alpha_{\mathrm{year}_i}+x_i^\top\beta
\end{aligned}
}
\]


```{r}
# Define optimization variable
beta <- Variable(p)

# Define fitted values
y_hat <- X %*% beta

# Define the annual GDP constraints. Scaling each equality by its target
# improves numerical conditioning without changing the feasible set.
constraints <- lapply(seq_along(years), function(i) {
  idx <- which(year == years[i])
  sum_entries(population[idx] * y_hat[idx]) / target_gdp[i] == 1
})

# Define constrained least-squares problem
problem <- Problem(
  Minimize(sum_squares(y - y_hat)),
  constraints
)

# Solve
result <- solve(problem, solver = "CLARABEL")

print(result$status)

if (result$status %in% c("optimal", "optimal_inaccurate")) {
  beta_hat <- value(beta)
  predictions <- as.vector(X %*% beta_hat)

  yearly_check <- data.frame(
    year = years,
    predicted_total_grdp = sapply(years, function(t) {
      idx <- which(year == t)
      sum(population[idx] * predictions[idx])
    }),
    target_total_grdp = target_gdp
  )

  yearly_check$difference <-
    yearly_check$predicted_total_grdp -
    yearly_check$target_total_grdp

  print(beta_hat)
  print(yearly_check)
  print(result$value)
} else {
  stop(sprintf("Constrained regression failed with solver status: %s", result$status))
}
```


### Statistical Summary

For observation \(i=1,\ldots,n\), let \(y_i\) be the observed GRDP per capita,
\(\hat y_i^{(C)}\) the constrained-model prediction, and
\(\hat y_i^{(OLS)}\) the ordinary least-squares prediction. The response mean
and total sum of squares are
\[
\bar y = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i,
\qquad
\mathrm{SST} = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\bar y)^2.
\]

The coefficient of determination is computed for each model as
\[
R_C^2
= 1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(C)})^2}{\mathrm{SST}},
\qquad
R_{OLS}^2
= 1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(OLS)})^2}{\mathrm{SST}}.
\]

The root mean squared error (RMSE), in GRDP-per-capita units, is
\[
\mathrm{RMSE}_C
=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(C)})^2},
\qquad
\mathrm{RMSE}_{OLS}
=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(OLS)})^2}.
\]

The RMSE difference and its absolute percentage relative to OLS are
\[
\Delta\mathrm{RMSE}
=\mathrm{RMSE}_C-\mathrm{RMSE}_{OLS},
\qquad
\%\mathrm{Difference}
=\frac{|\mathrm{RMSE}_C-\mathrm{RMSE}_{OLS}|}
{\mathrm{RMSE}_{OLS}}\times 100\%.
\]
A positive \(\Delta\mathrm{RMSE}\) means the constrained model's RMSE is higher;
a negative value means it is lower.

```{r}
ols_fit <- lm.fit(x = X, y = y)
ols_predictions <- as.vector(X %*% ols_fit$coefficients)

total_sum_squares <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
if (total_sum_squares == 0) {
  stop("Cannot compute R-squared because the observed response has zero variance.")
}

constrained_residuals <- y - predictions
ols_residuals <- y - ols_predictions

model_stats <- data.frame(
  model = c("Constrained", "Ordinary least squares"),
  R_squared = c(
    1 - sum(constrained_residuals^2) / total_sum_squares,
    1 - sum(ols_residuals^2) / total_sum_squares
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    sqrt(mean(constrained_residuals^2)),
    sqrt(mean(ols_residuals^2))
  )
)

print(model_stats, row.names = FALSE)

constrained_rmse <- model_stats$RMSE[model_stats$model == "Constrained"]
ols_rmse <- model_stats$RMSE[model_stats$model == "Ordinary least squares"]
cat(sprintf(
  "Constrained RMSE is %.6f GRDP-per-capita units (%.2f%%) %s than OLS RMSE.\n",
  abs(constrained_rmse - ols_rmse),
  abs(constrained_rmse - ols_rmse) / ols_rmse * 100,
  if (constrained_rmse >= ols_rmse) "higher" else "lower"
))
```

### Training fit and residual diagnostics

The first figure compares fitted values with observed training values for both
the constrained model and the ordinary least-squares reference. The diagnostic
panels examine residual patterns against fitted values and predictors,
approximate normality, residual spread, and differences across years. These are
visual checks rather than formal hypothesis tests. Because the constrained
model imposes annual weighted-sum equalities, its residuals are not the
independent, identically distributed residuals assumed by standard OLS
inference; interpret the plots as diagnostics, not as a basis for unadjusted
OLS significance tests.

```{r training-diagnostics, echo=FALSE}
training_diagnostics <- data.frame(
  province = regression_data$province,
  year = year,
  actual = y,
  constrained_fitted = predictions,
  constrained_residual = constrained_residuals,
  ols_fitted = ols_predictions,
  ols_residual = ols_residuals,
  year_factor = factor(year),
  mean_radiance = regression_data$mean_radiance,
  population = population,
  pixel_count = regression_data$pixel_count
)

dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("data/training_data", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

positive_residual_observations <- training_diagnostics[
  training_diagnostics$constrained_residual > 0,
  c(
    "province",
    "year",
    "actual",
    "constrained_fitted",
    "constrained_residual",
    "mean_radiance",
    "population",
    "pixel_count"
  )
]
positive_residual_observations <- positive_residual_observations[
  order(positive_residual_observations$constrained_residual, decreasing = TRUE),
]
write.csv(
  positive_residual_observations,
  "data/training_data/linear_model_positive_residual_observations.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
cat("Training observations with actual GRDP per capita above fitted values:\n")
print(head(positive_residual_observations, 10), row.names = FALSE)

actual_fitted_path <- "figures/linear_model_training_actual_vs_fitted.png"
grDevices::png(actual_fitted_path, width = 1800, height = 1100, res = 160)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
plot(
  training_diagnostics$actual,
  training_diagnostics$constrained_fitted,
  xlab = "Actual GRDP per capita",
  ylab = "Fitted GRDP per capita",
  main = "Training observations: actual vs fitted",
  pch = 19,
  col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#0072B2", alpha.f = 0.65),
  xlim = range(training_diagnostics$actual),
  ylim = range(
    training_diagnostics$constrained_fitted,
    training_diagnostics$ols_fitted
  )
)
points(
  training_diagnostics$actual,
  training_diagnostics$ols_fitted,
  pch = 1,
  col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#D55E00", alpha.f = 0.65)
)
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "gray35")
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = c("Constrained model", "OLS reference", "Perfect fit"),
  pch = c(19, 1, NA),
  lty = c(NA, NA, 2),
  col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "gray35"),
  bty = "n"
)
grDevices::dev.off()
knitr::include_graphics(actual_fitted_path)
```

boxplot(

### 2025 Level-2 Predictions

The fitted model produces an initial prediction for each level-2 unit using the
2025 intercept and the same training-data means and standard deviations used
when fitting the model. Calibrate predictions so the sum of level-2 predicted
GRDP per capita times level-2 population equals the province's 2025 GRDP per
capita times its independently reported province-level population. Convert the
province-level population from thousands to people. Add a common adjustment
\(\delta_j\) to every level-2 prediction within province \(j\):
\[
\tilde y_{ij} = \hat y_{ij} + \delta_j,
\qquad
\delta_j =
\frac{g_jN_j
-\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}\hat y_{ij}}
{\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}},
\]
where \(g_j\) is the province's 2025 GRDP per capita and \(P_{ij}\) is the
population of level-2 unit \(i\), and \(N_j\) is the reported total population
of province \(j\). Consequently,
\[
\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}\tilde y_{ij}
=g_jN_j.
\]

```{r}
if (anyNA(prediction_data$year) || any(prediction_data$year != 2025)) {
  stop("The level-2 prediction dataset must contain only 2025 observations.")
}
if (any(!complete.cases(prediction_data[, c(
  "name", "level_1", "population", "mean_radiance", "pixel_count"
)]))) {
  stop("The level-2 prediction data contains missing required values.")
}
prediction_features <- as.matrix(prediction_data[feature_columns])
if (any(!is.finite(prediction_features))) {
  stop("Level-2 prediction features must be finite.")
}
if (any(prediction_data$population < 0)) {
  stop("Level-2 populations must be finite and non-negative.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(paste(prediction_data$level_1, prediction_data$name, sep = "\r"))) {
  stop("The level-2 prediction data contains duplicate units within a province.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(provincial_grdp_data$province)) {
  stop("Provincial GRDP data contains duplicate province targets.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(provincial_population_data$province)) {
  stop("Provincial population data contains duplicate province totals.")
}

grdp_pc_2025 <- provincial_grdp_data[["2025"]][
  match(prediction_data$level_1, provincial_grdp_data$province)
]
if (anyNA(grdp_pc_2025) || any(!is.finite(grdp_pc_2025))) {
  stop("Missing or non-finite 2025 GRDP-per-capita target for a prediction province.")
}
province_population_2025 <- provincial_population_data[["2025"]][
  match(prediction_data$level_1, provincial_population_data$province)
] * 1000
if (anyNA(province_population_2025) ||
    any(!is.finite(province_population_2025)) ||
    any(province_population_2025 <= 0)) {
  stop("Missing or invalid 2025 population total for a prediction province.")
}

prediction_data$year_factor <- factor(prediction_data$year, levels = years)
for (feature in feature_columns) {
  scaled_feature <- paste0(feature, "_scaled")
  prediction_data[[scaled_feature]] <-
    (prediction_data[[feature]] - feature_means[[feature]]) /
    feature_sds[[feature]]
}

prediction_X <- model.matrix(
  ~ 0 + year_factor + mean_radiance_scaled + population_scaled +
    pixel_count_scaled,
  data = prediction_data
)
if (!identical(colnames(prediction_X), colnames(X))) {
  stop("Prediction design matrix does not match the fitted model.")
}

raw_level2_predictions <- as.vector(prediction_X %*% beta_hat)
province_names <- sort(unique(prediction_data$level_1))
province_adjustments <- setNames(numeric(length(province_names)), province_names)

for (province in province_names) {
  idx <- which(prediction_data$level_1 == province)
  level2_population <- sum(prediction_data$population[idx])
  if (!is.finite(level2_population) || level2_population <= 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Province %s has no positive level-2 population.", province))
  }

  province_index <- match(province, prediction_data$level_1)
  target_total <- grdp_pc_2025[province_index] *
    province_population_2025[province_index]
  raw_total <- sum(
    prediction_data$population[idx] * raw_level2_predictions[idx]
  )
  province_adjustments[[province]] <- (target_total - raw_total) /
    level2_population
}

prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita <- raw_level2_predictions
prediction_data$province_adjustment <-
  province_adjustments[prediction_data$level_1]
prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita <-
  prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita + prediction_data$province_adjustment
prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025 <- grdp_pc_2025

province_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(province_names, function(province) {
  idx <- which(prediction_data$level_1 == province)
  province_index <- match(province, prediction_data$level_1)
  province_population <- province_population_2025[province_index]
  target_total <- prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025[idx[1]] *
    province_population
  predicted_total <- sum(
    prediction_data$population[idx] *
      prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita[idx]
  )

  data.frame(
    province = province,
    population = province_population,
    level2_population = sum(prediction_data$population[idx]),
    target_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025[idx[1]],
    target_total_grdp = target_total,
    predicted_total_grdp = predicted_total,
    difference = predicted_total - target_total
  )
}))

if (any(abs(province_check$difference) >
        1e-8 * pmax(abs(province_check$target_total_grdp), 1))) {
  stop("Calibrated level-2 predictions do not match all provincial GDP targets.")
}

level2_predictions <- data.frame(
  level_2 = prediction_data$name,
  level_1 = prediction_data$level_1,
  year = prediction_data$year,
  population = prediction_data$population,
  province_population_2025 = province_population_2025,
  raw_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita,
  province_adjustment = prediction_data$province_adjustment,
  predicted_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita,
  province_grdp_per_capita_target_2025 =
    prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025
)
prediction_output <- "data/predicted_data/level2_grdp_pc_predictions.csv"
write.csv(level2_predictions, prediction_output, row.names = FALSE)

print(province_check, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Wrote level-2 predictions to", prediction_output, "\n")
head(level2_predictions)
```
